questions.q: What does ERC-721 represent, per the real OpenZeppelin GameItem example in this lesson?
options: A standard for fungible tokens only, like a currency
A contract that can only ever mint exactly one token total
Non-fungible, one-of-a-kind tokens, where each tokenId is distinct with its own owner and metadata
A deprecated standard no longer recommended by OpenZeppelin
questions.explain: ERC-721 is the standard for unique, one-of-a-kind tokens -- each tokenId is distinct, unlike a fungible currency token.

questions.q: What makes ERC-1155 different from ERC-721, per the GameItems example shown?
options: A single contract can manage many token types at once, each identified by its own id, fungible or not
ERC-1155 can only represent exactly one token type per contract, like ERC-721
ERC-1155 has no concept of a token id at all
ERC-1155 cannot be used for in-game items
questions.explain: The GameItems example shows GOLD (a large fungible quantity) and THORS_HAMMER (quantity of exactly 1) managed in the same ERC-1155 contract.

questions.q: Why does safeBatchTransferFrom save gas compared to repeated ERC-721 safeTransferFrom calls?
options: It eliminates all gas costs for NFT transfers entirely
It is slower but cheaper per transaction in total
It only works for a single token type at a time, same as ERC-721
It sends multiple token types in a single transaction, paying one transaction fee instead of several
questions.explain: Batching multiple token types into one call means one transaction fee covers what would otherwise require several separate ERC-721-style transfers.

questions.q: How does balanceOf differ between ERC-721 and ERC-1155, per this lesson?
options: They are identical function signatures with no differences
ERC-721's balanceOf takes only an address; ERC-1155's balanceOf takes an address and a specific token id
ERC-1155 has no balanceOf function at all
ERC-721's balanceOf requires a token id but ERC-1155's does not
questions.explain: ERC-721: balanceOf(address owner). ERC-1155: balanceOf(address, uint256) -- balance is tracked per address AND per token id.

questions.q: Per this lesson's guidance, which project would best fit ERC-1155 rather than ERC-721?
options: A game that needs gold, swords, shields, and other item types all managed efficiently in one contract
A single 1-of-1 piece of generative art with unique provenance
A deed representing ownership of one unique real-world property
A collection where every token must be completely unique with no shared type
questions.explain: ERC-1155 fits well when a project needs many token types (fungible, semi-fungible, or unique) managed together and often transferred/minted in batches, like game items.
